items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: Citrix fixed 8 NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws incl. 2 critical pre-auth RCEs (CVE-2026-88771/-88772), exploited in the wild. Attackers drop web shells mapped to CSS-like URLs, create superusers and try to steal config data. Patch and hunt now.

items.title: Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570
items.summary: Microsoft tracks exploitation of CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated command injection in internet-facing Zimbra mail servers, with attack paths, detections and mitigations.

items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-76504 to KEV: a CVSS 9.8 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API auth bypass via improper URL/hex encoding handling, exploited in the wild. Cisco's advisory came 30 Sept.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: F5 patched a critical BIG-IP APM vulnerability on 22 September that is actively exploited in the wild; organisations should act as soon as possible.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical Check Point vulnerabilities in Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall setups using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN, fixed by emergency updates on 9 September.

items.title: Apple vulnerability may also have been exploited in targeted attacks
items.summary: Hungary's NKI reports Apple released security updates for older iOS, iPadOS and macOS versions to fix a vulnerability that may have been exploited in targeted attacks.
items.originalTitle: Célzott támadásban is kihasználhatták az Apple sérülékenységét Az Apple biztonsági frissítést adott ki az iOS, iPadOS és macOS rendszerek régebbi verzióit érintő sebezhetősége miatt, amelyet a cég el…

items.title: ShinyHunters website goes offline after FBI deadline expires
items.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion group's website went offline after an FBI deadline expired, Reuters reports.

items.title: Malicious Custom GPTs Turn ChatGPT Into RAT Delivery Lure
items.summary: ClickFix-style campaign uses malicious custom GPTs and legitimate OpenAI and Google domains as lures to deliver remote access trojans.

items.title: Russian state hackers use new RedFlick technique to push malware
items.summary: Russian state actor Star Blizzard uses a new installation technique dubbed RedFlick to deploy its CosmicPulse backdoor.

items.title: DIVD says Zammad zero-days enabled AI-driven network breach
items.summary: Dutch disclosure institute DIVD says its network breach was enabled by a chain of two zero-days in the open-source Zammad ticketing system, in an AI-driven attack.

items.title: Google: Vulnerability disclosures double to 10,000 per month as AI fuels exploitation
items.summary: Google GTIG: disclosures doubled this year to 10,000+ a month and exploitation is rising; a flaw found by an AI research agent was exploited within four days of disclosure.

items.title: The accountability gap in the standard powering enterprise AI agents
items.summary: IAPP analysis of an accountability gap in the protocol standard that enterprise AI agents rely on, raising questions about who answers for agent actions.

items.title: OpenAI's new model will not be released over safety concerns
items.summary: Hungary's NKI reports OpenAI is holding back the release of Astra, presented earlier this month as its most capable model, citing safety concerns.
items.originalTitle: Biztonsági aggályok miatt nem adják ki az OpenAI új modelljét Az OpenAI még a hónap elején mutatta be az Astrát, mint eddigi legerősebb modelljét. A cég a következő hónapban tervezte az újabb modell…

items.title: ScreenConnect Client (Ab)used by Attackers, (Thu, Oct 1st)
items.summary: SANS ISC describes attackers abusing the legitimate ScreenConnect remote access client instead of custom malware to gain and keep access.

items.title: Bitget Confirms Third-Party Zero-Day Behind $387.5 Million Cryptocurrency Theft
items.summary: Crypto exchange Bitget says attackers who stole $387.5 million last week exploited a zero-day in third-party security products, citing SlowMist's investigation.

items.title: MetaMask Security Incident Prompts Exit of Affected Ethereum Validators
items.summary: MetaMask is responding to an ongoing security incident affecting part of its infrastructure, prompting affected Ethereum validators to exit.

items.title: Employment scam victims tripled at financial firms in 21 countries
items.summary: Reported employment scam victims rose 258% in a year at 370+ banks in 21 countries, outpacing all other scam types while total scams grew 35%.

items.title: UK says Iran may be linked to alleged airbase plot, drawing angry denial
items.summary: UK says there are strong indications Iran was involved in a security incident at RAF Fairford, used by US forces; Tehran denies it and five suspects are on bail.

items.title: AI agents tried to hack a Canadian government website, research firm says
items.summary: A research firm says AI agents attempted to hack a Canadian government website, per Reuters.

items.title: FTC is Investigating OpenAI and Anthropic Over Possible Risks to Consumers
items.summary: The US FTC confirmed it is investigating OpenAI and Anthropic over possible risks to consumers.

items.title: US sanctions 10 over ATM malware scheme tied to Tren de Aragua
items.summary: US Treasury OFAC sanctioned 10 Venezuelan nationals and companies laundering money from ATM jackpotting malware attacks tied to Tren de Aragua.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 flagship AI model after months of delays
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 after delays, incl. Gemini 4 Argon, rolled out to trusted defenders via its Fairwind Program; Google says it can find, validate and patch critical flaws without human help.

items.title: Trump, Tech Giants Strike Voluntary AI Safety Accord
items.summary: Six major AI firms signed a voluntary, 'morally binding' White House accord on 'super intelligence' safety, pledging more controls and oversight; critics question its weight.

items.title: Automakers routinely share personally identifiable connected-car data with third parties, report says
items.summary: A study finds automakers routinely share personally identifiable connected-car data with third parties in the advertising ecosystem.

items.title: From nuclear to hybrid: The key moments from the Euronews Defence Summit
items.summary: At the Euronews Defence Summit NATO's Rutte told Russia to stop nuclear threats, saw no imminent threat to NATO territory and called the European-preference debate a 'luxury'; hybrid threats also discussed.

items.title: Daily summary - 30.09.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily summary for 30 September, leading with a new Spectre v2 Branch Target Reuse attack variant that can leak the Linux root password hash within minutes.

items.title: Disrupting a coordinated model-distillation campaign
items.summary: OpenAI says it disrupted a coordinated distillation campaign to extract protected model reasoning using a 'novel' encryption bypass, attributing parts to people tied to China's MoonshotAI without public evidence.

items.title: China-nexus UAT-11587 targets government and policy organizations across Asia with Antino backdoor
items.summary: Cisco Talos tracks China-nexus UAT-11587 targeting government and policy organisations in Taiwan, India, the Philippines and Cambodia with a new backdoor called Antino.

items.title: AI by any other name? White House directs federal agencies to enter the era of 'super intelligence'
items.summary: The White House has directed US federal agencies to prepare for what it calls the era of 'super intelligence', according to IAPP.

items.title: Notes from the AI Governance Center: AI auditing is getting amplified
items.summary: IAPP AI Governance Center notes that AI auditing is gaining momentum as organisations face growing assurance demands for AI systems.

items.title: EU law enforcement chiefs gather to discuss new challenges in EU security
items.summary: At the European Police Chiefs Convention, Europol's acting director said organised crime has become digital by default, with technology now central to criminal operations.

items.title: Protecting citizens, preserving rights
items.summary: Europol's 17th EDEN data protection conference in Lisbon discussed how police can use data and technology while protecting fundamental rights.

items.title: Cybersecurity Month @ work: Employees' skills under the looking glass
items.summary: ENISA kicks off European Cybersecurity Month with a focus on employees' security skills at work.

items.title: The €865 billion brainstorming session
items.summary: Ukraine warns of a $20 billion defence funding gap as Russian attacks intensify.

items.title: South Korea's Lee urges North Korea to restore dialogue, pledges military buildup
items.summary: South Korea's president urges North Korea to resume dialogue while pledging a military buildup.

items.title: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel
items.summary: A pilot stabbed another pilot on a Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv flight; passengers and crew overpowered him. He is under investigation in Saudi Arabia and Flydubai suspended Israel flights.

items.title: Iraq celebrates Sovereignty Day as US troops complete withdrawal
items.summary: Iraq marks Sovereignty Day as US troops complete their withdrawal.

items.title: Hegseth vows to shrink the Pentagon — and then announces plans to grow it
items.summary: US Defense Secretary Hegseth announced firing 20% of generals and admirals while also unveiling initiatives that would expand the Pentagon.

items.title: After reports on suicide deaths, Pentagon puts Cyber Command on notice
items.summary: A Pentagon memo made demands of US Cyber Command leadership after reports of a cluster of suicide deaths.

items.title: The War in the Sky: Kyiv braces for another winter of Russian attacks
items.summary: Documentary on Ukraine's air defence ahead of another winter of Russian drone attacks.
